text:
maya: Quick check-in — proposal to simplify service auth incrementally. idea: introduce a thin "proxy token" that maps to existing project-scoped API keys, enforce least-privilege at runtime, and phase out broad long-lived keys. start with read-only scopes and roll up. thoughts?

alex: TL;DR yes — we need a low-friction migration for infra and apps. can you sketch the mapping model?

maya: sketch: proxy token holds {actor_id, allowed_routes, scope_hash} and is minted by auth-service after verifying original key. runtime enforces allowed_routes. no global wildcard unless opt-in. example mapping rule: 
```
# policy snippet
allow if token.actor == svc-x and route in ["/v1/models:infer","/v1/embeddings"]
```

sam: two immediate concerns: 1) telemetry / attribution — we must preserve original project id for billing, 2) performance — added hop could affect latency for hot paths.

irene: for (1) we can keep original_project in token metadata but strip it from downstream claims except billing. that lets runtime use local cache. for (2) consider local verification cache and signed short-lived tokens to avoid auth-service roundtrips on every request.

maya: yes — plan: mint short-lived proxy tokens (TTL 5m) signed by auth-service keypair. runtime validates signature + nonce in-memory. auth-service only needed for mint/rotation. initial rollout: mint tokens from gateway for inbound requests, runtime validates locally.

alex: how do we handle existing long-lived keys used by customers and internal services today? we need backward compatibility until migration completes.

maya: keep current keys working. migration phases:
1) opt-in: gateway can mint proxy tokens for calls using old key, issue header X-Proxy-Token, runtime accepts either old key or proxy token.
2) enforce: after opt-in window, runtime rejects requests presenting broad-scope old keys unless they present a proxy token. fallback path for emergency via admin toggle.
3) rotate: encourage staggered rotations, provide tooling for customers to create scoped tokens from console/CLI.

sam: rollout plan seems ok. add audit events for each mint and each rejection so we can track who/what depends on broad keys. also flag services that never present proxy tokens.

immediate question: how do we express per-route allowances without exploding policy size?

irene: use route-groups (e.g., embeddings.read = [/v1/embeddings, /v1/embeddings/batch]) and allow wildcard patterns with strict normalization. most services use a small set of groups.

maya: agreed. also add a compact representation for scope_hash so tokens stay small. token payload example: {aid:s-123, rg:[e,r], exp:1714104200, proj:proj-456, sig:..} (we'll base64).

alex: security review items: key compromise blast radius reduced? yes. will proxies introduce new secret storage needs? we'll rely on auth-service signing keys stored in KMS/HSM. runtime only needs public verification keys cached.

sam: another edge: internal async jobs that use long-running background clients. they can't re-mint every 5m easily. propose a tiered TTL: service-to-service tokens can be 12h but require stricter scope. admin-approval flow for exceptions.

maya: good point. we can support two classes: interactive (short TTL) and machine (longer TTL but limited to specific actor IDs + telemetry). require rotation enforcement and scheduled audits.

irene: ops: we'll need a rollout dashboard showing tokens minted per service, average TTLs, top rejected routes, and a migration heatmap. I'll pair with observability to add these metric tags.

alex: instrumentation should include original_key_id hashed so we don't leak customer keys in logs.

maya: yep — hash + salt in logs. also add a migration-mode header so we can track which calls are using proxy tokens vs legacy keys.

deploy-bot: canary minted proxy tokens in staging for svc-payment at 2024-09-12 15:04 :white_check_mark:

sam: next steps: draft RFC with migration phases, policy data model, token format, signing/rotation, and dashboard requirements. i'll own the rollout checklist. maya, can you draft model + token format?

maya: will do. I'll post a short RFC in docs/ and link here. aim to have draft by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — let's keep the opt-in window at least 4 weeks for internal consumers, longer for external customers.

irene: will start on metrics. also let's add an automated detector to surface services that still call wildcards after 2 weeks.

maya: note: this approach avoids touching RBAC data model initially — it's a runtime enforcement shim. later we can converge on unified RBAC grammar. but this gives a practical path to reduce blast radius now. :sparkles:
